summary: Greenwood County, SC lookout tower near Epworth: planned in a 1945 newspaper item, staffed in 1984, listed as removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed; no source gives a date or describes what, if anything, remains

events.note: Newspaper item on plans for lookout towers over 100 feet, one near Kinard's church in the Epworth community; completion not confirmed
A fire warden and his wife lived next to the Epworth Fire Tower; the wife was the tower operator
The SC Forestry Commission officially ended its tower network; the sources do not say when the Epworth tower came down

notes_for_editor: Two WebSearch calls and about three page reads. Almost everything about this tower comes from one page, Forest Lookouts, which quotes two Index-Journal items (November 22, 1945 and June 22, 1984), so the quotes are second-hand. The 1945 item describes plans; no source read confirms the tower was built, when, or to what design, so no built event is recorded. The Removed tag has no date. The 1993 network closure is a statewide fact from Columbia Metropolitan Magazine, not a source about this tower. A Greenwood County fire station (Epworth/Phoenix FD Station 70) appears in directory listings near Epworth, but no source ties it to the tower site, so it is left out. The brief's coordinates (34.1174, -82.026) were not checked. Access is unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 1945 item also says 'The management of the system is under county control', which the story does not address. The story no longer says who ran the towers; it reports only that the Forestry Commission ended its network in 1993, and a search of the magazine text found no mention of Greenwood, Epworth or Kinard. The 1993 claim is still the network's closure, not a record about this tower.
